# IMQOptions.publishSettleTime property

How long (ms) a clustered queue must have known a server before [ClusteredRedisQueue.publish()](/api/core/latest/core.clusteredredisqueue.publish/) prefers it as the one server an event goes to.

**Signature:**

```typescript
publishSettleTime?: number;
```

## Default Value

the `IMQ_PUBLISH_SETTLE_TIME` environment variable, or 7000

## Remarks

A clustered publish goes to one server, and reaches every subscriber only where each of them has already discovered that server and opened the channel on it. Subscribers discover a server at about the time the publisher does, but not at the same moment: a discovered server is therefore not preferred until it has been known this long. The default covers the UDP announcement interval (1 s) plus [UDPClusterManagerOptions.aliveTimeoutCorrection](/api/core/latest/core.udpclustermanageroptions.alivetimeoutcorrection/) (5 s) — the delay a manager already tolerates between two announcements it hears — plus one more interval for the subscription itself. Set it to match other intervals or corrections where your fleet uses them.

Servers listed in [IMQOptions.cluster](/api/core/latest/core.imqoptions.cluster/) are settled from the start: every process is configured with them, so nobody has to discover them. When no server has been known long enough — a process that has just started, say — any ready server is used. Ignored with [IMQOptions.publishFanOut](/api/core/latest/core.imqoptions.publishfanout/)<!-- -->.
